memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Israel asked, 'Why did you bring this trouble on me by telling the man you had another brother?' They replied, 'The man questioned us closely about ourselves and our family. "Is your father still living?" he asked us. "Do you have another brother?" We simply answered his questions. How were we to know he would say, "Bring your brother down here"?'" - Gen 43:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Facing the painful demand to send Benjamin, Jacob reaches for blame: "Why did you bring this trouble on me by telling the man you had another brother?" In his distress, he lashes out at his sons, as if their honest answers to the ruler's questions were the cause of all his grief. The brothers defend themselves — they had simply answered what they were asked.

This is a very human reaction to trouble. When we are hurting, fearful, or overwhelmed, we often look for someone to blame. It feels better, somehow, to pin our pain on another person than to sit in helpless distress. Jacob's grief was real, but his search for a scapegoat did not help; it only strained his relationship with his sons.

Blaming rarely solves anything. It does not remove the trouble, and it usually adds hurt and division to an already hard situation. When something goes wrong, our instinct to ask "Whose fault is this?" can consume energy that would be better spent asking "What do we do now?"

When you are in distress, watch that instinct to lash out and assign blame. The people around you are often not the true cause of your pain, and even when someone has genuinely erred, endless blame heals nothing. Bring your distress to God instead, and turn your energy toward the way forward. A blaming heart stays stuck; a trusting heart moves ahead.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When I'm hurting, do I look for someone to blame?
2. Does my blaming actually solve anything, or just add hurt?
3. Where do I need to move from "whose fault?" to "what now?"

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I am in distress, guard me from lashing out and looking for someone to blame. Help me to bring my pain to You instead, and to turn my energy toward the way forward. Amen.
